name: MediaLog
description: Everything you’ve watched, read, played, listened to, on one timeline.

facts.fact: Log films, books, shows, games, albums and podcasts.
Entries record when something was experienced and how it was.
See what the people you know have been into.
The supplied design groups its timeline into five-year periods and supports approximate dates.
Media types have distinct accent colours; navy typography sits on a pale blue-grey background.

artwork: New static vector symbols beside a consistent plain, licensed sans-serif wordmark converted to paths. Each symbol redraws one of collection 05’s ten styles around a book, with fewer details and no tile or border; user brand constraints override catalogue palettes and ornamental typography.
batch: Seventh compact logo set: the ten styles of collection 05, each redrawn as a simpler symbol built around a book, all static and free-standing.

brief.subject: MediaLog logo and brand title
brief.motif: Collection 05’s ten styles again, at the same 203 × 74 size and in the same output format, with a book in every symbol, less busy, and not every symbol on a tile or border.
brief.detail: Plain wordmark. Original static vector symbols readable at small size; no animation, ASCII or text-screen styles, tiny labels, neon cyan-pink pair or tagline. Light/dark and icon-only exports.

brand.typography: DejaVu Sans Bold, plain and consistent, outlined for portable SVGs

feedback.instruction: The MediaLog text does not need to be fancy.

feedback.source: User-shared feedback from Dan and Tim, 2026-10-10
feedback.instruction: Gently favour the book variant and dial back colours that evoke TikTok.
Book/pen/media heritage is a reference, not a requirement to copy the old mark.
Ten new random styles that have not already been made; no ASCII ones.
They do not have to look like the book/play/pen logo; be creative and cool. Keep the book theme when you can, but not every time.
Ten more, using the styles, but directed more towards media types: books, films, TV and so on.
Use the ten never-used styles: the last seven unused graphic styles plus three media-led styles (TV test card, pinball dot-matrix display, FM-synth keyboard display).
Ten more new ones, in the same output format as collection 05.
Focus a bit more on books in each one, and make them a little less busy; they do not all need a border around them.
Every unused style is a text-screen style, so repeat favourite graphic styles from earlier collections, redrawn around books.
Do collection 05’s ten again (shared its contact sheet), with the same steer as before: focus more on books in each one, make them a bit less busy, and they do not all need a border around them.
